title: Abstract DP168: Chronic Stroke Plasma Triggers Microglial Activation and Cognitive Decline in Young Mice

evidence_spans.quote: Results: Mice infused with chronic stroke plasma exhibited impairments in recognition memory
Blood plasma was collected from aged (18-month-old) male and female C57Bl/6 mice
Increased gliosis and senescent-like phenotypes were confirmed using immunohistochemistry.
Our ongoing work aims to identify the molecular mediators of these effects through multi-omic profiling.

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This empirical mouse study analyzes a confirmed senescent-like phenotype, but its multi-omic profiling is explicitly future work rather than part of the current report.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: Retro-orbital infusion of plasma from aged chronic-stroke donor mice
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Recognition and associative memory impairments; brain microglial activation and related inflammatory, mitochondrial, and senescence markers
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Outcomes in young recipients infused with chronic-stroke plasma versus sham plasma
